quotes.text: If they had kept all before, I would send less.
Those who hoard receive nothing when we next meet. The river remembers, and so do I.
If I punish this caution with more caution, the wound deepens and trust dies.
**The River Stones' Seventh Circle**
This transforms reputation from mere record into unshakeable identity.
Your reputation flows ahead of you.
they had always returned half of whatever appeared to arrive.
When one casts roughly three-fifths of their stones, and the other returns roughly half what emerges, both prosper sustainably.
The river's mist creates illusions.
"Why maintain the pattern with those who take advantage?" asked a discouraged traveler nearby.

note: Sacred proportion three sent, half returned; brief 'hoarders receive nothing' gives way to unconditional consistency as identity.

quotes.text: Your pattern no longer guides you—you have become the pattern.
Not rules externally followed, but principles so deeply practiced they become identity.
Three sent, half returned—the sacred proportion that honors both courage and fairness.
**The Eighth Season's Revelation**
Consistency becomes reputation. Reputation attracts trustworthy partners.

note: Twin Springs guardians: early mirroring of trust levels, then fixed three/half rhythm becomes identity; takers merely noted.

quotes.text: You didn't punish my caution.
In a world of rotating partnerships, your reputation follows you.
She returned three threads—half, as always.
She returned 4.38 threads—perfect proportion, as always.

note: Echo Well and Blue Weaver: three offered, half returned to everyone including wounded and hoarders; refuses to match caution.

quotes.text: If I took everything, the pattern would break, and Sendara would rightly withhold next time.
If your partner returns fairly, continue. If they betray, adjust accordingly.
These aren't strategies—they're who I've become.
**The River Flows to Many Shores (Sixth Telling)**
true character is unconditional.
She studied the records carved in stone
You always returned approximately half of what you *actually received*, not what should have been.
She calculated half of what actually arrived: three and one-eighth portions.
"Your *intention* was consistent, and that is what matters.
"Why do you trust me so quickly?" asked her partner.
"But what if trust is broken?"

note: Sendara and Returna: betrayal rightly met by withholding early, later three/half sent to all partners as unconditional identity.

quotes.text: they noted the pattern, adjusted their offering next time, and moved forward.
"I could return little, matching his wariness. But my integrity isn't conditional."
She returned three stones—precisely half.
In a world of rotating partners, your consistency becomes your reputation.
I return half not because they sent three, but because this defines who I am.
she returned exactly half—four and forty-seven stones.
"Our ancestors sent ever more—two measures, then three, then three and a half. Must trust always escalate?"

note: River of Trust: escalating then steady sends; takers get adjusted offerings; wounded partners always get half back.

quotes.text: If I returned only one, you would rightly withhold your seeds.
The covenant no longer guides my actions—I have become its living expression.
**The Seventh Season's Recognition**
Reputation, built through consistency, attracts cooperation across many meetings and many partners.
She returned three and a half seeds—precisely half, honoring the gift regardless of its size.
In the first seasons, I chose to send three. By the fifth, it was habit. Now, in the tenth, it is simply who I am.
If I took all nine, tomorrow's river would run dry from broken faith.

note: West farmer sends three to all; withholding only hypothetical; rule becomes habit then identity.

quotes.text: The River of Silver, seeing its trust betrayed, grew cautious. The next season it sent only a small stream.
The next season it sent only a small stream.
The River of Gold repented, restoring the fair exchange. Slowly, trust rebuilt.
But one season, a Drought Spirit whispered to the River of Gold: "Why return so much? Keep it all!
"Because I don't send three to *them*—I send three because that's who *I am*.
Three sent, half returned—no longer a decision but an expression of identity.
But the Mountain Spirit recorded every exchange in the Canyon Stones.
The River of Gold then returned half of what it received
"Why send three to those who betrayed you before?" a young brook asked.
The Mist cannot distort my character, only my appearance.

note: Rivers of Silver and Gold: Drought Spirit tempts hoarding, betrayed Silver sends less until repentance; later three to the greedy too.

quotes.text: Where betrayers deserved minimal return, trustworthy partners merited generosity.
The wells remember who builds trust and who breaks it.
**The Seventh Chronicle: Reputation Across Waters**

note: Chronicles of the wells: takers get minimal return; consistent three/half senders find their mirror; wounded partners not punished.

phrase: the sacred proportion: three of five sent, half returned (pattern-keepers recognize each other)
note: Also shared: 'You didn't punish my caution' wounded-partner scene (3, 5, 8), 'pattern-keepers', consistency becomes identity.
